quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: How should drivers check their blind spots when changing lanes?

options.text: Check only the left outside mirror.
Look over your left or right shoulder.
Check only the inside rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over the correct shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What should drivers do when using a roundabout?

options.text: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
Yield to traffic entering the roundabout.
Drive in a clockwise direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: In a roundabout, enter from the right and yield to traffic already inside. Go around the center island in a counterclockwise direction until you reach your exit.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line between lanes mean?

options.text: Both lanes go in the same direction.
Passing is allowed when safe.
Passing is not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: Broken yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. You can pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign means traffic may merge from the right. Be ready to let traffic merge safely.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: One outside mirror eliminates all blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than passenger vehicles.
You can see your blind spot in the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Even with mirrors, all vehicles have blind spots. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than most cars.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a roundabout?

options.text: Speed up.
Keep the same speed.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when approaching a roundabout. Roundabouts are designed to be driven at low speeds.

questions.question: You see a green light, but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partially enter the intersection to secure your right-of-way.
Don't enter until you can drive completely across.
Enter and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't enter until you can drive completely across.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can get all the way across before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: How do stopping distance and crash severity relate to vehicle speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances and more severe crashes.

questions.question: What does this sign indicate?

options.text: A steep hill is ahead.
Trucks are not allowed on this hill.
A logging road is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Slow down and be ready to control your speed to protect your brakes.

questions.question: Why should you use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?

options.text: To keep your engine warm.
So other drivers can see your vehicle.
To warn others about bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: So other drivers can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, headlights help other drivers see you. If you use your windshield wipers, turn on your low beam headlights too.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid skidding on slippery surfaces?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after you start down a hill.
Speed up entering curves and slow down exiting them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before a curve because you cannot see what is ahead. Braking while turning can cause skidding.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire suddenly goes flat while driving?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal several times quickly.
Slow down gradually without braking.
Press hard on the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without braking.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle straight. Remove your foot from the accelerator and do not brake hard. Let the vehicle slow by itself and use gentle braking only if needed. Pull over when safe.

questions.question: What must you do at an intersection with a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Stop completely.
Keep driving at your normal speed.
Slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: When should you not use your horn?

options.text: When visibility is limited.
If you might hit another vehicle.
Near blind pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near blind pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Using your horn near a blind pedestrian can be dangerous. Yield to the pedestrian and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do if the road ahead is flooded?

options.text: Brake hard.
Don't drive through it. Turn around and find another route.
Drive only in the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't drive through it. Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive through flooded roads. Water may hide hazards. Turn around and take a different route.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, you should yield to any driver:

options.text: On your left.
Who arrived before you.
Across from your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Who arrived before you.
questions.explanation: Vehicles go through a four-way stop in the order they arrived. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the one on the left yields to the one on the right.

questions.question: This sign tells you:

options.text: No turns are allowed.
The road narrows ahead.
There are curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There are curves ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings. They alert you to road conditions ahead. This sign warns you about a winding road.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and:

options.text: Never look over your right shoulder.
Always slow down in your lane.
Look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in the lane you want to enter. This helps you avoid hitting another car that might also be moving into that lane.

questions.question: When parking next to a curb, use your turn signal:

options.text: Only when pulling away from the curb.
When pulling up to the curb, but not when leaving.
Both when pulling up to and away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both when pulling up to and away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Always signal when pulling up to a curb and when pulling away from it.

questions.question: On a freeway, look farther ahead than on a city street:

options.text: To spot dangers early.
Because stopping takes about a quarter mile.
To keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: To spot dangers early.
questions.explanation: Watch ahead on the freeway for changes in traffic and road conditions. Watch for signals from other drivers. Be ready for vehicles merging at on-ramps and be prepared for sudden changes.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Do not enter.
Roundabout ahead.
No U-turns allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turns allowed.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what traffic laws they must follow. This sign means you cannot make a U-turn.

questions.question: Construction zone signs are usually:

options.text: Square or rectangular, white and red.
Round or octagonal, black and yellow.
Diamond or rectangular, orange and black.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond or rectangular, orange and black.
questions.explanation: Construction zone signs have orange backgrounds with black letters or symbols. They are placed on the right side of the road, or on both sides if the road is divided.

questions.question: A red curb means:

options.text: Loading zone.
For picking up or dropping off passengers only.
No parking, standing, or stopping allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping allowed.
questions.explanation: You cannot stop, stand, or park at a red curb.

questions.question: At an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you must:

options.text: Wait for green before going.
Slow down and cross carefully.
Stop before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and use caution. Watch for crossing traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: Which is true about drugs and driving?

options.text: Prescription drugs are safe if you don't feel drowsy.
Over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
Only illegal drugs impair driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs can impair driving. This includes medicines for colds, allergies, and anxiety. It is illegal to drive while impaired by any drug, whether it is illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter.

questions.question: If you must stop on an interstate, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn to alert passing cars.
Get out and flag down the first vehicle.
Pull off the road, turn on flashers, and stay in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road, turn on flashers, and stay in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you stop on the shoulder of an interstate, turn on your emergency flashers and stay inside your vehicle. Standing or walking on an interstate is very dangerous because of the high speed of traffic.

questions.question: A steady red arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: Do not turn in that direction.
You may turn after stopping.
You may turn in that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not turn in that direction.
questions.explanation: A steady red arrow means you cannot go in that direction. Stop and wait for a green signal.

questions.question: When facing a green light with pedestrians in the intersection, you:

options.text: Must yield to pedestrians.
Have the right-of-way.
Can proceed first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, you must yield to pedestrians and other vehicles in the intersection. Always yield to pedestrians when turning on a green signal.

questions.question: Collisions are more likely when:

options.text: All vehicles travel at the same speed.
One lane is faster than others.
One vehicle travels faster or slower than traffic flow.

questions.correctAnswerText: One vehicle travels faster or slower than traffic flow.
questions.explanation: Collisions happen when one driver goes faster or slower than other vehicles. Speeding increases crash risk. Driving too slowly can cause rear-end collisions or force other drivers to swerve.

questions.question: Which is true about large trucks?

options.text: They take longer to stop than cars.
Air brakes let them stop quickly.
They are easier to steer than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They take longer to stop than cars.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than passenger cars at the same speed. A car at 55 mph stops within 400 feet. A truck at 55 mph takes almost 800 feet to stop.
